messages:
maria: heads-up — the sample app for the ESM SDK is failing TypeScript checks when run on the edge runtime. getting TS2345 about fetch types and also weird overload resolution. anyone seen this today?

alex: hmm, saw something similar in a user repro yesterday. quick guess: tsconfig module/moduleResolution mismatch between NodeNext and classic node16 - the emitted d.ts differ for default vs named export interop.

sophie: can you paste the error and the function signature? overload issues often come from how we declare the generic overloads for createClient. sometimes `unknown` vs `any` causes inference to fail.

maria: error snippet: `Argument of type 'RequestInit' is not assignable to parameter of type 'Request'` and `No overload matches this call.` It's during a call to our `client.chat.generate<T>` helper inside an edge function. We build ESM with `module: "ESNext"` in the sample tsconfig.

alex: that fetch error smells like TS libs mismatch — edge runtime uses DOM lib fetch types, node ESM uses lib dom or lib dom.iterable if you add it. if the package d.ts expects `node-fetch`'s types you'll get incompat. For the overloads: we have two signatures, one generic and one fallback. TS sometimes prefers the non-generic if inference fails.

sophie: here's a minimal problematic overload pattern we had:```ts
export function generate<T extends Output = Output>(opts: GenerateOptions<T>): Promise<T>
export function generate(opts: GenerateOptions): Promise<Output>
```
If the compiler can't infer T from opts (because of `unknown` fields) it picks the second overload. Using a single generic with defaults or making the generic parameter inferable from a property helps.

jamal: also flag: the edge build strips node types and the package ships both cjs and esm declarations. our rollup/tsc pipeline was emitting declarations twice into dist/cjs and dist/esm and npm clients pick the wrong one depending on resolver. that can cause the consumer TS to see different signatures.

maria: ugh, that explains why the local dev ESM sample works but the hosted example on the edge preview fails. difference in how Next/Edge resolver picks up `types`/`exports`.

alex: short-term: add `"types": "dist/esm/index.d.ts"` in package.json for the sample app or publish corrected types. long-term: we should make the package's generated types consistent across formats — emit a single canonical types bundle and point package.json types to it.

sophie: for the `unknown` vs `any` part — we deliberately used `unknown` in a few places to force explicit casts in user code. that makes inference tricky for overloads. suggest: keep `unknown` in runtime-safety layers but provide thin wrapper types in the SDK entry that map to `any` or more inferable shapes for DX.

jamal: note for runtime parity: the ESM build was missing our default retry middleware in one config path — likely tree-shaken when built with the bundler because it looked side-effect-free. that changes runtime behavior (auth/retry differences) between CJS and ESM installs. we need a smoke test that validates auth+retry across both package entries on edge.

maria: can someone open a tiny PR that: (1) pins package.json types to esm bundle, (2) adjusts overloads to be inferable, and (3) adds a CI smoke test for edge ESM? I'll triage.

alex: I'll take the types pin + docs note about tsconfig for sample apps. PR in a few hours.

sophie: I'll propose a small typing change: collapse the pair of overloads into a single signature with conditional inference, or add a helper `InferOutput<T>` so TS can always derive the generic. I'll open a draft.

jamal: I'll add an IAM-auth+retry sample run to the edge matrix and trigger full test on the PR.

ci-bot: build triggered for branch alex/esm-types-pin (job 4821) :rocket:

maria: thanks all — this is blocking a customer smoke test so high priority. we should also add a note to the onboarding quickstart about recommended tsconfig settings for edge: `{"module":"ESNext","moduleResolution":"bundler","lib":["DOM","ES2021"],"esModuleInterop":true}` to reduce surprises.

alex: agreed — and add `skipLibCheck: true` as pragmatic workaround until we canonicalize types.

sophie: small FYI — collapse of overloads reduced one internal test, but I validated with DTS tests that user inference improves in the sample app. I'll link tests in the PR.

maria: perfect. i'll keep this thread updated when the customer passes their smoke test. :thumbsup:
